[Source](https://docs.rs/src/data_encoding/lib.rs.html#1327-1335)#### pub fn [encode_len](https://docs.rs#method.encode_len)(&self, len: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/data_encoding/lib.rs.html#1327-1335)

#### pub fn [encode_len](https://docs.rs#method.encode_len)(&self, len: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

Returns the encoded length of an input of length `len`

See [ encode_mut](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html#method.encode_mut) for when to use it.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

May panic if `len` is greater than `usize::MAX / 512`:

- `len <= 8_388_607`when- `target_pointer_width = "32"`
- `len <= 36028_797018_963967`when- `target_pointer_width = "64"`

If you need to encode an input of length greater than this limit (possibly of infinite
length), then you must chunk your input, encode each chunk, and concatenate to obtain the
output. The length of each input chunk must be a multiple of [ encode_align](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html#method.encode_align).

Note that this function only *may* panic in those cases. The function may also return the
correct value in some cases depending on the implementation. In other words, those limits
are the guarantee below which the function will not panic, and not the guarantee above which
the function will panic.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/data_encoding/lib.rs.html#1546-1558)#### pub fn [decode_len](https://docs.rs#method.decode_len)(&self, len: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), [DecodeError](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/data_encoding/lib.rs.html#1546-1558)

#### pub fn [decode_len](https://docs.rs#method.decode_len)(&self, len: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), [DecodeError](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeError.html)>

Returns the maximum decoded length of an input of length `len`

See [ decode_mut](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html#method.decode_mut) for when to use it. In particular, the actual decoded length might be
smaller if the actual input contains padding or ignored characters.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

May panic if `len` is greater than `usize::MAX / 8`:

- `len <= 536_870_911`when- `target_pointer_width = "32"`
- `len <= 2_305843_009213_693951`when- `target_pointer_width = "64"`

If you need to decode an input of length greater than this limit (possibly of infinite
length), then you must decode your input chunk by chunk with [ decode_mut](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html#method.decode_mut), making sure
that you take into account how many bytes have been read from the input and how many bytes
have been written to the output:

- `Ok(written)`means all bytes have been read and- `written`bytes have been written
- `Err(DecodePartial { error, .. })`means an error occurred if- `error.kind != DecodeKind::Length`or this was the last input chunk
- `Err(DecodePartial { read, written, .. })`means that- `read`bytes have been read and- `written`bytes written (the error can be ignored)

Note that this function only *may* panic in those cases. The function may also return the
correct value in some cases depending on the implementation. In other words, those limits
are the guarantee below which the function will not panic, and not the guarantee above which
the function will panic.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-2)Errors

Returns an error if `len` is invalid. The error kind is [ Length](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeKind.html#variant.Length) and the

[position](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeError.html#structfield.position)is the greatest valid input length.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/data_encoding/lib.rs.html#1598-1608)#### pub fn [decode_mut](https://docs.rs#method.decode_mut)(
    &self,
    input: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
    output: &mut [[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), [DecodePartial](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodePartial.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/data_encoding/lib.rs.html#1598-1608)

#### pub fn [decode_mut](https://docs.rs#method.decode_mut)(
    &self,
    input: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
    output: &mut [[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), [DecodePartial](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodePartial.html)>

Decodes `input` in `output`

Returns the length of the decoded output. This length may be smaller than the output length if the input contained padding or ignored characters. The output bytes after the returned length are not initialized and should not be read.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-5)Panics

Panics if the `output` length does not match the result of [ decode_len](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html#method.decode_len) for the

`input`
length. Also panics if `decode_len` fails for the `input` length.[§](https://docs.rs#errors-3)Errors

Returns an error if `input` is invalid. See [ decode](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html#method.decode) for more details. The are two
differences though:

- `Length`- `decode_len`
- The `read``written`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
use data_encoding::BASE64;
let input = b"SGVsbA==byB3b3JsZA==";
let output = &mut buffer[0 .. BASE64.decode_len(input.len()).unwrap()];
let len = BASE64.decode_mut(input, output).unwrap();
assert_eq!(&output[0 .. len], b"Hello world");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/data_encoding/lib.rs.html#1640-1645)**crate feature **`alloc` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/data_encoding/lib.rs.html#1640-1645)

**crate feature**only.

`alloc`Returns decoded `input`

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-4)Errors

Returns an error if `input` is invalid. The error kind can be:

- `Length`- [position](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeError.html#structfield.position)is the greatest valid input length.
- `Symbol`- [position](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeError.html#structfield.position)is the first invalid character.
- `Trailing`- [position](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeError.html#structfield.position)is the first character containing non-zero trailing bits.
- `Padding`- [position](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeError.html#structfield.position)is the first padding character of the first padding of invalid length.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use data_encoding::BASE64;
assert_eq!(BASE64.decode(b"SGVsbA==byB3b3JsZA==").unwrap(), b"Hello world");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/data_encoding/lib.rs.html#1672-1691)#### pub fn [is_canonical](https://docs.rs#method.is_canonical)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/data_encoding/lib.rs.html#1672-1691)

#### pub fn [is_canonical](https://docs.rs#method.is_canonical)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Returns whether the encoding is canonical

An encoding is not canonical if one of the following conditions holds:

- trailing bits are not checked
- padding is used
- characters are ignored
- characters are translated

# data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/index.html

## Expand description

Efficient and customizable data-encoding functions like base64, base32, and hex

This [crate](https://crates.io/crates/data-encoding) provides little-endian ASCII base-conversion encodings for
bases of size 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. It supports:

- [padding](https://docs.rs/struct.Specification.html#structfield.padding)for streaming
- canonical encodings (e.g. [trailing bits](https://docs.rs/struct.Specification.html#structfield.check_trailing_bits)are checked)
- in-place [encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html#method.encode_mut)and[decoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html#method.decode_mut)functions
- partial [decoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html#method.decode_mut)functions (e.g. for error recovery)
- character [translation](https://docs.rs/struct.Specification.html#structfield.translate)(e.g. for case-insensitivity)
- most and least significant [bit-order](https://docs.rs/struct.Specification.html#structfield.bit_order)
- [ignoring](https://docs.rs/struct.Specification.html#structfield.ignore)characters when decoding (e.g. for skipping newlines)
- [wrapping](https://docs.rs/struct.Specification.html#structfield.wrap)the output when encoding
- no-std environments with `default-features = false, features = ["alloc"]`
- no-alloc environments with `default-features = false`

You may use the [binary](https://crates.io/crates/data-encoding-bin) or the [website](https://data-encoding.rs) to play around.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

This crate provides predefined encodings as [constants](https://docs.rs/index.html#constants). These constants are of type
[ Encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html). This type provides encoding and decoding functions with in-place or allocating
variants. Here is an example using the allocating encoding function of

[:](https://docs.rs/constant.BASE64.html)

`BASE64````
use data_encoding::BASE64;
assert_eq!(BASE64.encode(b"Hello world"), "SGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=");
```
Here is an example using the in-place decoding function of [ BASE32](https://docs.rs/constant.BASE32.html):

```
use data_encoding::BASE32;
let input = b"JBSWY3DPEB3W64TMMQ======";
let mut output = vec![0; BASE32.decode_len(input.len()).unwrap()];
let len = BASE32.decode_mut(input, &mut output).unwrap();
assert_eq!(&output[0 .. len], b"Hello world");
```
You are not limited to the predefined encodings. You may define your own encodings (with the
same correctness and performance properties as the predefined ones) using the [ Specification](https://docs.rs/struct.Specification.html)
type:

```
use data_encoding::Specification;
let hex = {
    let mut spec = Specification::new();
    spec.symbols.push_str("0123456789abcdef");
    spec.encoding().unwrap()
};
assert_eq!(hex.encode(b"hello"), "68656c6c6f");
```
You may use the [macro](https://crates.io/crates/data-encoding-macro) library to define a compile-time custom encoding:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use data_encoding::Encoding;
use data_encoding_macro::new_encoding;
const HEX: Encoding = new_encoding!{
    symbols: "0123456789abcdef",
    translate_from: "ABCDEF",
    translate_to: "abcdef",
};
const BASE64: Encoding = new_encoding!{
    symbols: "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/",
    padding: '=',
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#properties)Properties

The [ HEXUPPER](https://docs.rs/constant.HEXUPPER.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/constant.BASE32.html)

`BASE32`[,](https://docs.rs/constant.BASE32HEX.html)

`BASE32HEX`[, and](https://docs.rs/constant.BASE64.html)

`BASE64`[predefined encodings conform to](https://docs.rs/constant.BASE64URL.html)

`BASE64URL`[RFC4648](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4648).

In general, the encoding and decoding functions satisfy the following properties:

- They are deterministic: their output only depends on their input
- They have no side-effects: they do not modify any hidden mutable state
- They are correct: encoding followed by decoding gives the initial data
- They are canonical (unless `is_canonical`

This last property is usually not satisfied by base64 implementations. This is a matter of
choice and this crate has made the choice to let the user choose. Support for canonical encoding
as described by the [RFC](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4648#section-3.5) is provided. But it is also possible to disable checking
trailing bits, to add characters translation, to decode concatenated padded inputs, and to
ignore some characters. Note that non-canonical encodings may be an attack vector as described
in [Base64 Malleability in Practice](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/361.pdf).

Since the RFC specifies the encoding function on all inputs and the decoding function on all
possible encoded outputs, the differences between implementations come from the decoding
function which may be more or less permissive. In this crate, the decoding function of canonical
encodings rejects all inputs that are not a possible output of the encoding function. Here are
some concrete examples of decoding differences between this crate, the `base64` crate, and the
`base64` GNU program:

| Input | `data-encoding` | `base64` | GNU `base64` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AAB=` | `Trailing(2)` | `Last(2)` | `\x00\x00` |
| `AA\nB=` | `Length(4)` | `Byte(2)` | `\x00\x00` |
| `AAB` | `Length(0)` | `Padding` | Invalid input |
| `AAA` | `Length(0)` | `Padding` | Invalid input |
| `A\rA\nB=` | `Length(4)` | `Byte(1)` | Invalid input |
| `-_\r\n` | `Symbol(0)` | `Byte(0)` | Invalid input |
| `AA==AA==` | `[0, 0]` | `Byte(2)` | `\x00\x00` |

We can summarize these discrepancies as follows:

| Discrepancy | `data-encoding` | `base64` | GNU `base64` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Check trailing bits | Yes | Yes | No |
| Ignored characters | None | None | `\n` |
| Translated characters | None | None | None |
| Check padding | Yes | No | Yes |
| Support concatenated input | Yes | No | Yes |

This crate permits to disable checking trailing bits. It permits to ignore some characters. It permits to translate characters. It permits to use unpadded encodings. However, for padded encodings, support for concatenated inputs cannot be disabled. This is simply because it doesn’t make sense to use padding if it is not to support concatenated inputs.

# BASE64 in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/constant.BASE64.html

`pub const BASE64: `[Encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html);## Expand description

Padded base64 encoding

This encoding is a static version of:

```
let mut spec = Specification::new();
spec.symbols.push_str("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/");
spec.padding = Some('=');
assert_eq!(BASE64, spec.encoding().unwrap());
```
It conforms to [RFC4648](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4648#section-4).

# HEXUPPER in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/constant.HEXUPPER.html

`pub const HEXUPPER: `[Encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html);## Expand description

Uppercase hexadecimal encoding

This encoding is a static version of:

```
let mut spec = Specification::new();
spec.symbols.push_str("0123456789ABCDEF");
assert_eq!(HEXUPPER, spec.encoding().unwrap());
```
It is compliant with [RFC4648](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4648#section-8) and known as “base16” or “hex”.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use data_encoding::HEXUPPER;
let deadbeef = vec![0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef];
assert_eq!(HEXUPPER.decode(b"DEADBEEF").unwrap(), deadbeef);
assert_eq!(HEXUPPER.encode(&deadbeef), "DEADBEEF");
```

# Encoder in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/struct.Encoder.html

`pub struct Encoder<'a> { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`alloc`## Expand description

Encodes fragmented input to an output

It is equivalent to use an [ Encoder](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoder.html) with multiple calls to

[than to first concatenate all the input and then use](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoder.html#method.append)

`Encoder::append()`[. In particular, this function will not introduce padding or wrapping between inputs.](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html#method.encode_append)

`Encoding::encode_append()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
// This is a bit inconvenient but we can't take a long-term reference to data_encoding::BASE64
// because it's a constant. We need to use a static which has an address instead. This will be
// fixed in version 3 of the library.
static BASE64: data_encoding::Encoding = data_encoding::BASE64;
let mut output = String::new();
let mut encoder = BASE64.new_encoder(&mut output);
encoder.append(b"hello");
encoder.append(b"world");
encoder.finalize();
assert_eq!(output, BASE64.encode(b"helloworld"));
```

# BitOrder in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/enum.BitOrder.html

```
pub enum BitOrder {
    MostSignificantFirst,
    LeastSignificantFirst,
}
```
**crate feature**only.

`alloc`## Expand description

Order in which bits are read from a byte

The base-conversion encoding is always little-endian. This means that the least significant
**byte** is always first. However, we can still choose whether, within a byte, this is the most
significant or the least significant **bit** that is first. If the terminology is confusing,
testing on an asymmetrical example should be enough to choose the correct value.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

In the following example, we can see that a base with the `MostSignificantFirst` bit-order has
the most significant bit first in the encoded output. In particular, the output is in the same
order as the bits in the byte. The opposite happens with the `LeastSignificantFirst` bit-order.
The least significant bit is first and the output is in the reverse order.

```
use data_encoding::{BitOrder, Specification};
let mut spec = Specification::new();
spec.symbols.push_str("01");
spec.bit_order = BitOrder::MostSignificantFirst;  // default
let msb = spec.encoding().unwrap();
spec.bit_order = BitOrder::LeastSignificantFirst;
let lsb = spec.encoding().unwrap();
assert_eq!(msb.encode(&[0b01010011]), "01010011");
assert_eq!(lsb.encode(&[0b01010011]), "11001010");
```
## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MostSignificantFirst)

### MostSignificantFirst

Most significant bit first

This is the most common and most intuitive bit-order. In particular, this is the bit-order
used by [RFC4648](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4648) and thus the usual hexadecimal, base64, base32, base64url, and base32hex
encodings. This is the default bit-order when [specifying](https://docs.rs/struct.Specification.html) a
base.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.LeastSignificantFirst)

### LeastSignificantFirst

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# BASE32HEX_NOPAD in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/constant.BASE32HEX_NOPAD.html

`pub const BASE32HEX_NOPAD: `[Encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html);## Expand description

Unpadded base32hex encoding

This encoding is a static version of:

```
let mut spec = Specification::new();
spec.symbols.push_str("0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUV");
assert_eq!(BASE32HEX_NOPAD, spec.encoding().unwrap());
```

---

# BASE32_DNSCURVE in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/constant.BASE32_DNSCURVE.html

`pub const BASE32_DNSCURVE: `[Encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html);## Expand description

DNSCurve base32 encoding

This encoding is a static version of:

```
let mut spec = Specification::new();
spec.symbols.push_str("0123456789bcdfghjklmnpqrstuvwxyz");
spec.bit_order = BitOrder::LeastSignificantFirst;
spec.translate.from.push_str("BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ");
spec.translate.to.push_str("bcdfghjklmnpqrstuvwxyz");
assert_eq!(BASE32_DNSCURVE, spec.encoding().unwrap());
```
It conforms to [DNSCurve](https://dnscurve.org/in-implement.html).

---

# BASE32_DNSSEC in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/constant.BASE32_DNSSEC.html

`pub const BASE32_DNSSEC: `[Encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html);## Expand description

DNSSEC base32 encoding

This encoding is a static version of:

```
let mut spec = Specification::new();
spec.symbols.push_str("0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv");
spec.translate.from.push_str("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUV");
spec.translate.to.push_str("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv");
assert_eq!(BASE32_DNSSEC, spec.encoding().unwrap());
```
It conforms to [RFC5155](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5155):

- It uses a base32 extended hex alphabet.
- It is case-insensitive when decoding and uses lowercase when encoding.
- It does not use padding.

---

# BASE64_MIME in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/constant.BASE64_MIME.html

`pub const BASE64_MIME: `[Encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html);## Expand description

MIME base64 encoding

This encoding is a static version of:

```
let mut spec = Specification::new();
spec.symbols.push_str("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/");
spec.padding = Some('=');
spec.wrap.width = 76;
spec.wrap.separator.push_str("\r\n");
assert_eq!(BASE64_MIME, spec.encoding().unwrap());
```
It does not exactly conform to [RFC2045](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2045) because it does not print the header
and does not ignore all characters.

---

# BASE64_MIME_PERMISSIVE in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/constant.BASE64_MIME_PERMISSIVE.html

`pub const BASE64_MIME_PERMISSIVE: `[Encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html);## Expand description

MIME base64 encoding without trailing bits check

This encoding is a static version of:

```
let mut spec = Specification::new();
spec.symbols.push_str("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/");
spec.padding = Some('=');
spec.wrap.width = 76;
spec.wrap.separator.push_str("\r\n");
spec.check_trailing_bits = false;
assert_eq!(BASE64_MIME_PERMISSIVE, spec.encoding().unwrap());
```
It does not exactly conform to [RFC2045](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2045) because it does not print the header
and does not ignore all characters.

---

# HEXLOWER in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/constant.HEXLOWER.html

`pub const HEXLOWER: `[Encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html);## Expand description

Lowercase hexadecimal encoding

This encoding is a static version of:

```
let mut spec = Specification::new();
spec.symbols.push_str("0123456789abcdef");
assert_eq!(HEXLOWER, spec.encoding().unwrap());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use data_encoding::HEXLOWER;
let deadbeef = vec![0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef];
assert_eq!(HEXLOWER.decode(b"deadbeef").unwrap(), deadbeef);
assert_eq!(HEXLOWER.encode(&deadbeef), "deadbeef");
```

---

# HEXLOWER_PERMISSIVE in data_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding/^2.11.0/constant.HEXLOWER_PERMISSIVE.html

`pub const HEXLOWER_PERMISSIVE: `[Encoding](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoding.html);## Expand description

Lowercase hexadecimal encoding with case-insensitive decoding

This encoding is a static version of:

```
let mut spec = Specification::new();
spec.symbols.push_str("0123456789abcdef");
spec.translate.from.push_str("ABCDEF");
spec.translate.to.push_str("abcdef");
assert_eq!(HEXLOWER_PERMISSIVE, spec.encoding().unwrap());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use data_encoding::HEXLOWER_PERMISSIVE;
let deadbeef = vec![0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef];
assert_eq!(HEXLOWER_PERMISSIVE.decode(b"DeadBeef").unwrap(), deadbeef);
assert_eq!(HEXLOWER_PERMISSIVE.encode(&deadbeef), "deadbeef");
```
You can also define a shorter name:

```
use data_encoding::{Encoding, HEXLOWER_PERMISSIVE};
const HEX: Encoding = HEXLOWER_PERMISSIVE;
```

# data_encoding_macro - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/data-encoding-macro/0.1.20/aarch64-apple-darwin/data_encoding_macro/

## Expand description

Macros for data-encoding

This library provides macros to define compile-time byte arrays from encoded strings (using
common bases like [base64](https://docs.rs/macro.base64.html), [base32](https://docs.rs/macro.base32.html), or [hexadecimal](https://docs.rs/macro.hexlower_permissive.html), and also custom bases). It also provides
a macro to define compile-time custom encodings to be used with the [data-encoding](https://crates.io/crates/data-encoding) crate at
run-time.

Up to Rust 1.50, you may need to add the following to your `.cargo/config.toml` to use this
library in no-std or no-alloc environments:

```
[unstable]
features = ["host_dep"]
```
From Rust 1.51, you may need to add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[package]
resolver = "2"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

You can define a compile-time byte slice from an encoded string literal:

```
const HELLO_SLICE: &'static [u8] = &data_encoding_macro::hexlower!("68656c6c6f");
const FOOBAR_SLICE: &'static [u8] = &data_encoding_macro::base64!("Zm9vYmFy");
```
You can also define a compile-time byte array from an encoded string literal:

```
data_encoding_macro::hexlower_array!("const HELLO" = "68656c6c6f");
data_encoding_macro::base64_array!("const FOOBAR" = "Zm9vYmFy");
```
You can define a compile-time custom encoding from its specification:

```
const HEX: data_encoding::Encoding = data_encoding_macro::new_encoding! {
    symbols: "0123456789abcdef",
    translate_from: "ABCDEF",
    translate_to: "abcdef",
};
const BASE64: data_encoding::Encoding = data_encoding_macro::new_encoding! {
    symbols: "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/",
    padding: '=',
};
```

# data_encoding_macro - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/data-encoding-macro/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/data_encoding_macro/index.html

## Expand description

Macros for data-encoding

This library provides macros to define compile-time byte arrays from encoded strings (using
common bases like [base64](https://docs.rs/macro.base64.html), [base32](https://docs.rs/macro.base32.html), or [hexadecimal](https://docs.rs/macro.hexlower_permissive.html), and also custom bases). It also provides
a macro to define compile-time custom encodings to be used with the [data-encoding](https://crates.io/crates/data-encoding) crate at
run-time.

Up to Rust 1.50, you may need to add the following to your `.cargo/config.toml` to use this
library in no-std or no-alloc environments:

```
[unstable]
features = ["host_dep"]
```
From Rust 1.51, you may need to add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[package]
resolver = "2"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

You can define a compile-time byte slice from an encoded string literal:

```

const FOOBAR_SLICE: &'static [u8] = &data_encoding_macro::base64!("Zm9vYmFy");

You can also define a compile-time byte array from an encoded string literal:

    padding: '=',

# data_encoding_macro/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Macros for data-encoding
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! This library provides macros to define compile-time byte arrays from encoded strings (using
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! common bases like [base64], [base32], or [hexadecimal], and also custom bases). It also provides
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! a macro to define compile-time custom encodings to be used with the [data-encoding] crate at
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! run-time.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//!
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! Up to Rust 1.50, you may need to add the following to your `.cargo/config.toml` to use this
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! library in no-std or no-alloc environments:
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//!
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! ```toml
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! [unstable]
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! features = ["host_dep"]
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! ```
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! From Rust 1.51, you may need to add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! ```toml
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! [package]
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! resolver = "2"
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! ```
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! # Examples
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! You can define a compile-time byte slice from an encoded string literal:
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! ```rust
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! const HELLO_SLICE: &'static [u8] = &data_encoding_macro::hexlower!("68656c6c6f");
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! const FOOBAR_SLICE: &'static [u8] = &data_encoding_macro::base64!("Zm9vYmFy");
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! # fn main() {}
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! ```
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! You can also define a compile-time byte array from an encoded string literal:
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! ```rust
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! data_encoding_macro::hexlower_array!("const HELLO" = "68656c6c6f");
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! data_encoding_macro::base64_array!("const FOOBAR" = "Zm9vYmFy");
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! # fn main() {}
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! ```
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! You can define a compile-time custom encoding from its specification:
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! ```rust
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! const HEX: data_encoding::Encoding = data_encoding_macro::new_encoding! {
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!     symbols: "0123456789abcdef",
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!     translate_from: "ABCDEF",
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!     translate_to: "abcdef",
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! };
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! const BASE64: data_encoding::Encoding = data_encoding_macro::new_encoding! {
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//!     symbols: "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/",
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!     padding: '=',
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! };
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! # fn main() {}
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! ```
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! [base32]: macro.base32.html
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! [base64]: macro.base64.html
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! [data-encoding]: https://crates.io/crates/data-encoding
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! [hexadecimal]: macro.hexlower_permissive.html
[60](https://docs.rs#60)
[61](https://docs.rs#61)#![no_std]
[62](https://docs.rs#62)#![warn(unused_results)]
[63](https://docs.rs#63)
[64](https://docs.rs#64)#[doc(hidden)]
[65](https://docs.rs#65)pub use data_encoding_macro_internal::{
[66](https://docs.rs#66)    internal_decode_array, internal_decode_slice, internal_new_encoding,
[67](https://docs.rs#67)};
[68](https://docs.rs#68)
[69](https://docs.rs#69)/// Defines a compile-time byte array by decoding a string literal
[70](https://docs.rs#70)///
[71](https://docs.rs#71)/// This macro takes a list of `key: value,` pairs (the last comma is required). It takes the
[72](https://docs.rs#72)/// key-value pairs specifying the encoding to use to decode the input (see [new_encoding] for the
[73](https://docs.rs#73)/// possible key-value pairs), the input itself keyed by `input`, and the output keyed by `name`.
[74](https://docs.rs#74)/// The output must be of the form `[pub] {const|static} <name>`.
[75](https://docs.rs#75)///
[76](https://docs.rs#76)/// # Examples
[77](https://docs.rs#77)///
[78](https://docs.rs#78)/// ```rust
[79](https://docs.rs#79)/// data_encoding_macro::decode_array! {
[80](https://docs.rs#80)///     name: "const OCTAL",
[81](https://docs.rs#81)///     symbols: "01234567",
[82](https://docs.rs#82)///     padding: '=',
[83](https://docs.rs#83)///     input: "237610==",
[84](https://docs.rs#84)/// }
[85](https://docs.rs#85)/// # fn main() {}
[86](https://docs.rs#86)/// ```
[87](https://docs.rs#87)///
[88](https://docs.rs#88)/// [new_encoding]: macro.new_encoding.html
[89](https://docs.rs#89)#[macro_export]
[90](https://docs.rs#90)macro_rules! decode_array {
[91](https://docs.rs#91)    ($($arg: tt)*) => {
[92](https://docs.rs#92)        $crate::internal_decode_array!($($arg)*);
[93](https://docs.rs#93)    };
[94](https://docs.rs#94)}
[95](https://docs.rs#95)
[96](https://docs.rs#96)/// Defines a compile-time byte slice by decoding a string literal
[97](https://docs.rs#97)///
[98](https://docs.rs#98)/// This macro takes a list of `key: value,` pairs (the last comma is required). It takes the
[99](https://docs.rs#99)/// key-value pairs specifying the encoding to use to decode the input (see [new_encoding] for the
[100](https://docs.rs#100)/// possible key-value pairs), the input itself keyed by `input`, and the output keyed by `name`.
[101](https://docs.rs#101)///
[102](https://docs.rs#102)/// # Examples
[103](https://docs.rs#103)///
[104](https://docs.rs#104)/// ```rust
[105](https://docs.rs#105)/// const OCTAL: &'static [u8] = &data_encoding_macro::decode_slice! {
[106](https://docs.rs#106)///     symbols: "01234567",
[107](https://docs.rs#107)///     padding: '=',
[108](https://docs.rs#108)///     input: "237610==",
[109](https://docs.rs#109)/// };
[110](https://docs.rs#110)/// # fn main() {}
[111](https://docs.rs#111)/// ```
[112](https://docs.rs#112)///
[113](https://docs.rs#113)/// [new_encoding]: macro.new_encoding.html
[114](https://docs.rs#114)#[macro_export]
[115](https://docs.rs#115)macro_rules! decode_slice {
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    ($($arg: tt)*) => {
[117](https://docs.rs#117)        $crate::internal_decode_slice!($($arg)*)
[118](https://docs.rs#118)    };
[119](https://docs.rs#119)}
[120](https://docs.rs#120)
[121](https://docs.rs#121)/// Defines a compile-time custom encoding
[122](https://docs.rs#122)///
[123](https://docs.rs#123)/// This macro takes a list of `key: value,` pairs (the last comma is required). The possible
[124](https://docs.rs#124)/// key-value pairs are:
[125](https://docs.rs#125)///
[126](https://docs.rs#126)/// ```text
[127](https://docs.rs#127)///             symbols: <string>,       // e.g. "01234567"
[128](https://docs.rs#128)///             padding: [None]|<char>,  // e.g. '='
[129](https://docs.rs#129)///           bit_order: [MostSignificantFirst]|LeastSignificantFirst,
[130](https://docs.rs#130)/// check_trailing_bits: [true]|false,
[131](https://docs.rs#131)///              ignore: [""]|<string>,  // e.g. " \t\n"
[132](https://docs.rs#132)///          wrap_width: [0]|<int>,      // e.g. 76
[133](https://docs.rs#133)///      wrap_separator: [""]|<string>,  // e.g. "\r\n"
[134](https://docs.rs#134)///      translate_from: [""]|<string>,  // e.g. "ABCDEF"
[135](https://docs.rs#135)///        translate_to: [""]|<string>,  // e.g. "abcdef"
[136](https://docs.rs#136)/// ```
[137](https://docs.rs#137)///
[138](https://docs.rs#138)/// Only `symbols` is required. Everything else is optional and defaults to the value between square
[139](https://docs.rs#139)/// brackets.
[140](https://docs.rs#140)///
[141](https://docs.rs#141)/// # Examples
[142](https://docs.rs#142)///
[143](https://docs.rs#143)/// ```rust
[144](https://docs.rs#144)/// const HEX: data_encoding::Encoding = data_encoding_macro::new_encoding! {
[145](https://docs.rs#145)///     symbols: "0123456789abcdef",
[146](https://docs.rs#146)///     ignore: " \r\t\n",
[147](https://docs.rs#147)///     wrap_width: 32,
[148](https://docs.rs#148)///     wrap_separator: "\n",
[149](https://docs.rs#149)///     translate_from: "ABCDEF",
[150](https://docs.rs#150)///     translate_to: "abcdef",
[151](https://docs.rs#151)/// };
[152](https://docs.rs#152)/// # fn main() {}
[153](https://docs.rs#153)/// ```
[154](https://docs.rs#154)#[macro_export]
[155](https://docs.rs#155)macro_rules! new_encoding {
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    ($($arg: tt)*) => {
[157](https://docs.rs#157)        data_encoding::Encoding::internal_new(&$crate::internal_new_encoding!{ $($arg)* })
[158](https://docs.rs#158)    };
[159](https://docs.rs#159)}
[160](https://docs.rs#160)
[161](https://docs.rs#161)macro_rules! make {
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    ($base: ident $base_array: ident = $ref: ident; $($spec: tt)*) => {
[163](https://docs.rs#163)        #[macro_export]
[164](https://docs.rs#164)        macro_rules! $base_array {
[165](https://docs.rs#165)            ($n: tt = $x: tt) => {
[166](https://docs.rs#166)                $crate::decode_array!(name: $n, input: $x, $($spec)*);
[167](https://docs.rs#167)            };
[168](https://docs.rs#168)        }
[169](https://docs.rs#169)        #[macro_export]
[170](https://docs.rs#170)        macro_rules! $base {
[171](https://docs.rs#171)            ($x: tt) => {
[172](https://docs.rs#172)                $crate::decode_slice!(input: $x, $($spec)*)
[173](https://docs.rs#173)            };
[174](https://docs.rs#174)        }
[175](https://docs.rs#175)        #[test]
[176](https://docs.rs#176)        fn $base() {
[177](https://docs.rs#177)            assert_eq!(new_encoding!($($spec)*), data_encoding::$ref);
[178](https://docs.rs#178)        }
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    };
[180](https://docs.rs#180)}
[181](https://docs.rs#181)

# decode_array in data_encoding_macro - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/data-encoding-macro/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/data_encoding_macro/macro.decode_array.html

```
macro_rules! decode_array {
    ($($arg: tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Defines a compile-time byte array by decoding a string literal

This macro takes a list of `key: value,` pairs (the last comma is required). It takes the
key-value pairs specifying the encoding to use to decode the input (see [new_encoding](https://docs.rs/macro.new_encoding.html) for the
possible key-value pairs), the input itself keyed by `input`, and the output keyed by `name`.
The output must be of the form `[pub] {const|static} <name>`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
data_encoding_macro::decode_array! {
    name: "const OCTAL",
    symbols: "01234567",
    padding: '=',
    input: "237610==",
}
```

---

# decode_slice in data_encoding_macro - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/data-encoding-macro/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/data_encoding_macro/macro.decode_slice.html

```
macro_rules! decode_slice {
    ($($arg: tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Defines a compile-time byte slice by decoding a string literal

This macro takes a list of `key: value,` pairs (the last comma is required). It takes the
key-value pairs specifying the encoding to use to decode the input (see [new_encoding](https://docs.rs/macro.new_encoding.html) for the
possible key-value pairs), the input itself keyed by `input`, and the output keyed by `name`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
const OCTAL: &'static [u8] = &data_encoding_macro::decode_slice! {
    symbols: "01234567",
    padding: '=',
    input: "237610==",
};
```

# new_encoding in data_encoding_macro - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/data-encoding-macro/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/data_encoding_macro/macro.new_encoding.html

```
macro_rules! new_encoding {
    ($($arg: tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Defines a compile-time custom encoding

This macro takes a list of `key: value,` pairs (the last comma is required). The possible
key-value pairs are:

```
            symbols: <string>,       // e.g. "01234567"
            padding: [None]|<char>,  // e.g. '='
          bit_order: [MostSignificantFirst]|LeastSignificantFirst,
check_trailing_bits: [true]|false,
             ignore: [""]|<string>,  // e.g. " \t\n"
         wrap_width: [0]|<int>,      // e.g. 76
     wrap_separator: [""]|<string>,  // e.g. "\r\n"
     translate_from: [""]|<string>,  // e.g. "ABCDEF"
       translate_to: [""]|<string>,  // e.g. "abcdef"
```
Only `symbols` is required. Everything else is optional and defaults to the value between square
brackets.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
const HEX: data_encoding::Encoding = data_encoding_macro::new_encoding! {
    symbols: "0123456789abcdef",
    ignore: " \r\t\n",
    wrap_width: 32,
    wrap_separator: "\n",
    translate_from: "ABCDEF",
    translate_to: "abcdef",
};
```
